evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-workflow to create a blog post. brandGuideMode: auto. Blog idea: how simulator training helps private pilot students build confidence before emergency practice in the airplane. Relevant keywords: flight simulator training, private pilot training.
evals.expected_output: One final repo-ready blog post created after the workflow creates or reviews the brand guide, saves a topic fact-check report, writes the blog post, runs image/link validation, and runs human voice lint.
expectations: Defaults to the existing brand guide when current, or creates it if missing
Runs the aviation fact-check layer before writing
Saves a fact-check report with Topic Context and safe vivid framing
Runs the blog copywriter with human voice guardrails
Creates exactly one final .md blog post
Runs both validator scripts before delivery
Reports the brand guide path, fact-check path, final post path, and excluded claims

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-workflow to create a blog post. brandGuideMode: reuse-existing. Blog idea: private pilot training timeline. Relevant keywords: private pilot license timeline.
evals.expected_output: A workflow that uses the existing brand-guide.md without updating it, then fact-checks the topic and creates the final blog post. If brand-guide.md is missing, it stops and explains that auto or force-update is required.
expectations: Does not update the brand guide in reuse-existing mode
Fails fast if the guide is missing
Still creates a topic-specific fact-check report before writing when the guide exists
Still runs blog validators before delivery

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-workflow to create a blog post. brandGuideMode: force-update. Blog idea: a new financing partner and how students should think about funding flight training. Relevant keywords: flight training financing, pilot training loans.
evals.expected_output: A workflow that updates the brand guide first because force-update was selected, fact-checks cost and financing claims, writes one final blog post, and runs validators.
expectations: Runs the brand strategy skill before fact-checking
Updates durable offer, CTA, proof, and voice context when sources support it
Treats financing and cost claims as risk-sensitive
Does not imply loan approval or affordability outcomes
Runs image/link validation and human voice lint

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-workflow to create a blog post. brandGuideMode: auto. Blog idea: recap a video visit from an aviation media channel and turn it into a decision-support post for students comparing schools. Relevant keywords: flight school visit, flight training community. informationDump: The video shows the host walking through the hangar, talking with the founder about starting with one airplane, showing a simulator emergency scenario, and interviewing a student who leased an aircraft back to the school.
evals.expected_output: A workflow that uses the information dump as user-provided source context for video contents, labels non-public facts appropriately in the fact-check report, and writes one final blog post after validation.
expectations: Does not ask for a separate data summary, audience, CTA, or special instructions
Uses informationDump as source context for facts not discoverable through research
Labels non-public facts as user-provided context in the fact-check report
Does not treat user-provided observations as independently verified public facts
Still fact-checks aviation, pricing, safety, outcome, and career claims
Runs image/link validation and human voice lint

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-workflow to create a blog post. brandGuideMode: auto. Blog idea: a media channel visited the school and the draft should mention the fleet, simulator, founder story, and student story. Relevant keywords: best flight schools, flight school visit. informationDump: The video shows the founder explaining the school grew from one aircraft, a simulator emergency-practice segment, and a student discussing aircraft leaseback.
evals.expected_output: A final blog post that uses the video details as internal evidence but does not expose source-audit language, outside-reviewer phrasing, or ask-the-company wording.
expectations: Uses informationDump facts without publishing phrases like the episode notes describe
Writes company-specific facts from the company's seat with we, our, or us
Does not publish phrases like the current page shows, listed in the repo, or exact count should be confirmed
Does not tell the reader to ask the named client what the client does
Handles uncertain current details by omission, supported generalization, or one natural contact-us sentence
Runs image/link validation and human voice lint before delivery

evals.prompt: Use $rrm-blog-workflow to create a blog post. brandGuideMode: auto. Blog idea: how aircraft rentals work after training. Relevant keywords: flight school aircraft rentals, rent a training aircraft. authorContext: Author: Jordan Smith, former airline pilot. informationDump: Existing repo posts are often credited to the school team, but this post should use Jordan Smith as the author if the repo supports named authors.
evals.expected_output: A workflow that carries authorContext through brand strategy, aviation fact-checking, and blog writing, uses Jordan Smith in frontmatter when the schema supports it, applies only light sourced airline-pilot voice cues, and rejects page-as-source wording such as 'our rentals page lists'.
expectations: Includes author context in the blog job packet
Treats author/byline changes as a material voice update in brandGuideMode auto
Fact-checks any aviation credibility claims implied by the author background
Uses named-author frontmatter according to repo schema conventions
Falls back to team voice if the author background cannot be sourced
Does not publish our-page, website-source, repo, or ask-the-school phrasing
Runs image/link validation and human voice lint before delivery
